_provenance.honest_status: RECONSTRUCTED, NOT A BYTE-FOR-BYTE RECORDING. No export file was available on this machine and one cannot be produced without a consented LinkedIn account. The sheet names, the label/value shape of DISCOVERY and FOLLOWERS, the header text of ENGAGEMENT and TOP POSTS, and the side-by-side dual-table layout of TOP POSTS (cols 0-2 ranked by engagements, cols 4-6 ranked by impressions, spacer column between) were triangulated from three independent open-source parsers that were each written against a real export.
sources: https://github.com/juliettech13/personal-analytics web/lib/uploads/parse.ts (documents the note+blank preamble above the TOP POSTS header)
https://github.com/altafshaikh/content-factory .claude/skills/linkedin-performance-agent/SKILL.md (confirms Engagements is a composite with no breakdown)
_provenance.replace_with_real_file: When a genuine export arrives, dump each sheet with openpyxl iter_rows(values_only=True) into this same shape and rerun tests/test_linkedin_export.py. Any header LinkedIn has renamed will fail loudly here rather than writing nulls into the corpus.
deliberate_variations: Block 2's date header is 'Post Publish Date' while block 1's is 'Post publish date': both casings have been observed in the wild.
The same post appears in both tables with different utm tracking parameters, which is why merging happens on the activity id and not the URL string.
Three date encodings are present on purpose: a real datetime cell, an m/d/yyyy string, and an Excel serial number.
Three post-id shapes are present on purpose: /posts/...-activity-<id>, urn:li:activity:<id>, and a /pulse/ article with no id at all.

cell_encoding: Plain JSON scalars become string/number/blank cells. {"__dt__": "<iso>"} becomes a real datetime cell, which is what openpyxl hands back for a date-formatted column.
